title: Where the Ocean's Salt Really Comes From
post_title: Where the Ocean's Salt Really Comes From | QuantaTale
post_description: The two sources of ocean salt and how much of seawater is salt, from NOAA and USGS. Sources: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/whysalty.html and United States Geological Survey https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/saline-water-and-salinity #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: Where does all the ocean's salt come from? It comes from two places: runoff from land and openings in the seafloor. Slightly acidic rainwater erodes rocks on land. That frees ions, which rivers carry to the sea. Hydrothermal fluids from vents in the seafloor add more. Sodium and chloride make up most of the ocean's dissolved ions. Even so, only a small share of seawater's weight is dissolved salt. In the extremely salty Dead Sea, the dense water holds you up like a mattress.
